solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Prison officer goes to club for cocktail

parts.note: screw is slang for a prison warder
a driver is a golf club

explanation.surface: A warder heads off to a nightclub for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a nightspot, but it is the golf club. 'goes to' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A vodka and orange juice mix is the classic drink of this name.

clue.text: Shock subject for play school

definitions.meaning: an outrage that causes public shock
Sheridan's play The School for ... takes it as its subject

explanation.surface: A startling topic for a children's play group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play school' reads as a nursery; it really points to the comedy The School for Scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrageous conduct that shocks the public is called this; the Sheridan comedy names it in its title.

clue.text: Two rivers characteristic of the country

parts.note: R is the usual abbreviation for river
the Ural is a river flowing from Russia through Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: Two rivers sum up the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Countryside life as opposed to town life is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Going crazy with a wine list may eventually affect this

definitions.text: Going crazy with a wine list may eventually affect this

indicators.note: letters going crazy are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Overindulging from the wine list will show around your middle in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going crazy' rearranges A WINE LIST; the whole clue then describes where heavy drinking ends up showing.
explanation.definitionFit: The girth of the body at the middle grows with overindulgence in drink.

clue.text: Drums sound to start a revolution

definitions.meaning: a drum ... is the rapid beating of drums
to set something rotating or turning over

explanation.surface: A drumbeat signals the uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests a political uprising; here it is a turning motion.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapid drumbeat has this name, and the verb means to turn over and over.

clue.text: Shipping company after vessel for petroleum product

indicators.note: the shipping company piece is placed after the vessel piece

parts.note: a vase is a vessel for flowers
a line is a company running ships

explanation.surface: A shipping firm follows a tanker carrying oil products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship alongside the shipping company, but it is a flower vase.
explanation.definitionFit: Petroleum jelly sold under this brand name is a refined petroleum derivative.

clue.text: He was known for loving capital, nothing more

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A man famed for his love of a capital city and nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loving capital' reads as a love of money or a city; 'loving' belongs to the definition. 'more' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's lovestruck hero, whose name now stands for any ardent male lover.

clue.text: Organ bright with flowers

parts.note: the nose is the organ of smell
gay in its old sense of bright, colourful

explanation.surface: A church organ made colourful with floral decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the church instrument; it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bouquet of fragrant blooms is a posy of this name.

clue.text: Is jesting about providing support on flight

indicators.note: the jesting word goes about, around, the word Is

parts.note: banter is playful jesting talk
taken as written

explanation.surface: Joking around while giving someone moral support during a plane journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests air travel; it is a flight of stairs. 'providing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A handrail running beside a staircase supports people climbing it.

clue.text: Aid fliers being diverted to find places to land

indicators.note: letters being diverted are sent off in a new order

explanation.surface: Relief pilots are rerouted to look for landing sites.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft touch down at these sites with runways.

clue.text: Intends to get sufficient funds

definitions.meaning: to have in mind as a purpose
money or resources enough to live on, as in a person of independent wealth

explanation.surface: Plans to raise enough money.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is to signify or intend; the plural noun is income or wealth.

clue.text: Returning, I'd delayed to explain more fully

indicators.note: the word I'd comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
late means delayed, behind time

explanation.surface: Back again, someone excuses their lateness with a fuller explanation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' suggests coming back late; it only turns the short word round. 'delayed' sits naturally beside it to disguise the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To expand or enlarge on a topic, speaking at length about it.

clue.text: Admitting whole sum is due

parts.note: all means the entire amount
owing means still to be paid

explanation.surface: Confessing the entire amount is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Granting or conceding, as in letting someone in, is a synonym.

clue.text: Fast, the Italian's pulse

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian fasting diet relying on beans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' looks like a heartbeat, but it is an edible seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible seeds of legumes such as peas, beans and this lens-shaped seed are called pulses.

clue.text: 4 Managed to raise local taxes and provides an account

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word reads it upwards, backwards

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
rates were the British local property taxes

explanation.surface: A council succeeded in raising its taxes and publishes a report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to raise' turns RAN into NAR. RATES were local property taxes in Britain, replaced in 1990 for homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling a story or giving a spoken account of events is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Holding north, top fighter pilots attempt descent

indicators.note: the pilots piece holds the north letter inside it

parts.note: aces are star fighter pilots
try means attempt

explanation.surface: Elite pilots heading north try to make a landing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'descent' suggests an aircraft coming down; it means lineage.
explanation.definitionFit: Family line or lineage, one's descent from forebears.

clue.text: No cure, sadly — time for support

indicators.note: the words No cure go sadly, badly, into another order

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: With no cure, sadly, it is time to offer comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' looks like the mood of the sentence after 'No cure', but it is the anagram signal for those two words; the dash just separates the time piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To back or hearten someone is to give them support.

clue.text: Not the favourite in society?

parts.note: a rank long shot in a race; with a wry query, someone the social set does not let in

explanation.surface: Someone unpopular in the social world.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second sense: someone excluded from society.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse with long odds, or a person excluded from a group, both have this name.

clue.text: French port or claret

definitions.meaning: a major port on the Garonne in south-west France

explanation.surface: A French harbour town or its red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' may suggest the fortified wine beside 'claret'; it is a harbour city. 'or' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The city gives its name to the wine region whose red wines Britons call claret.

clue.text: Withdrawing support?

explanation.surface: Pulling out of helping someone.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about withdrawn help, but splits into two meanings that look opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both going backwards and giving financial endorsement.

clue.text: He had high-flying ambition but came unstuck

definitions.text: He had high-flying ambition but came unstuck

parts.words: He had high-flying ambition but came unstuck
parts.note: the Greek youth who flew too near the sun so the wax holding his wings melted

explanation.surface: A man of lofty ambitions who failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came unstuck' is literal: the wax on his wings melted.
explanation.definitionFit: The myth of Daedalus's son is the archetype of overreaching ambition ending in a fall.

clue.text: Reliable way to limit bloodshed

definitions.meaning: to stem a flow of blood from a wound

explanation.surface: A dependable method to reduce violent killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloodshed' suggests war; it means literal bleeding. 'way' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyal supporter is described this way; the verb means to stop bleeding, also spelt stanch.

clue.text: Sign's sensible yet not in a straightforward way

parts.note: the Crab is the zodiac sign Cancer
wise means sensible

explanation.surface: An astrological sign is smart, but devious.
explanation.walkthrough: ''s' and 'yet' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving sideways like a crab, hence indirectly or obliquely.

clue.text: Women's group left — street's hoisted flags

parts.note: WI is the Women's Institute, a British community organisation

indicators.note: in a down clue, hoisting lifts the word upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A women's club has left, and banners are raised along the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hoisted' turns ST into TS. The WI (Women's Institute) is a British community club for women.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that droop or energy that fades both mean to weaken, as this verb does.

clue.text: Breaking up coal for furnace

indicators.note: breaking the words up coal smashes their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Smashing coal into pieces to feed a furnace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furnace' sounds like a definition of fire; a cupola is a vertical furnace for melting iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupola furnace is a cylindrical shaft furnace used in foundries to melt iron.

clue.text: Rosie's willowy form

definitions.note: willowy is an adjective, while the answer is a noun naming a willow tree

indicators.note: Rosie's letters take a new form

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Rosie has a slender figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'willowy form' reads as a slender figure; 'willowy' hints at a kind of willow and 'form' rearranges ROSIE.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a species of willow whose flexible twigs are used in basketwork.

clue.text: No success keeping a girl quiet

parts.note: Flo is a girl's name, short for Florence
P is piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: A failure to keep a young woman silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' is a link word joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete failure, as of a show that bombs, is a synonym.

clue.text: I give a hand, being perfect!

parts.note: to deal is to give out a hand of cards

explanation.surface: Someone helping out claims to be faultless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give a hand' suggests helping; it means distributing cards. 'being' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Flawless or exactly as wished, a model of excellence.

clue.text: This pet may sleep indoors but its quarters are hardly spotless

definitions.text: This pet may sleep indoors but its quarters are hardly spotless

parts.words: This pet may sleep indoors but its quarters are hardly spotless
parts.note: a house dog whose whole body, its quarters, is covered in spots

explanation.surface: A pet that sleeps inside but keeps a messy bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' looks like living space; it means the animal's own body, which is spotted.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of dog known for its white coat with black or liver spots.

clue.text: Chief follows priests out for personal inspection

indicators.note: the chief piece follows the rearranged priests
the letters of priests are out of their order

parts.note: arch means chief, principal

explanation.surface: A head clergyman comes after some priests who have been ejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like the priests being ejected, but it signals their letters being rearranged; 'follows' puts the chief piece last.
explanation.definitionFit: A search of someone's body after removing their clothes, as at customs or in prison.
